analysis.statement: RAG systems often retrieve irrelevant or off‑topic passages, which then propagate into hallucinated or unsupported generations.
Current training objectives do not explicitly enforce that the generated text aligns with the retrieved evidence, leading to factual inconsistency.
Zero‑shot dense retrievers such as HyDE assume a unimodal query distribution and struggle with ambiguous queries, a limitation shared by many retrieval‑augmented generators.
Both lines of work note that off‑the‑shelf retrieval models, trained on knowledge‑intensive tasks, are sub‑optimal for open‑ended or instruction‑following generation.
The reliance on numerical relevance scores may be unnecessary if the language model can directly assess passage usefulness, suggesting a shared inefficiency across methods.

directions.title: Joint Retrieval‑Generation Training with Consistency Loss
directions.rationale: If RAG models are trained to explicitly maximize alignment between generated tokens and retrieved passages, factual consistency should improve. This addresses the lack of explicit training to follow facts (E3) and the off‑topic retrieval issue (E2).
directions.validation_experiment: Dataset: NaturalQuestions + generated answer verification; Baseline: standard SELF‑RAG; Metric: Fact‑Consistency (FEVER score) and BLEU.

directions.title: Ambiguity‑Aware Retrieval via Multi‑Modal Query Modeling
directions.rationale: HyDE’s unimodal assumption (E5) limits handling of ambiguous queries. Introducing a mixture‑of‑experts query encoder can capture multiple possible intents, reducing retrieval of irrelevant passages and benefiting open‑ended generation.
directions.validation_experiment: Dataset: Ambiguous query set from MS‑MARCO; Baseline: HyDE; Metric: Retrieval Recall@10 and downstream generation factuality.

directions.title: Instruction‑Tuned Retrieval Models for Open‑Ended Generation
directions.rationale: Off‑the‑shelf retrievers underperform for instruction following (E4). Fine‑tuning retrieval models on instruction‑style data should produce more on‑topic passages, mitigating hallucinations.
directions.validation_experiment: Dataset: Alpaca‑style instruction prompts with reference passages; Baseline: vanilla DPR; Metric: Retrieval relevance (MRR) and generation ROUGE.

directions.title: Eliminating Explicit Relevance Scores via End‑to‑End NLU Scoring
directions.rationale: If strong NLU/NLG models can directly judge passage usefulness (E9), the system can drop dense similarity scoring, simplifying the pipeline and possibly improving robustness.
directions.validation_experiment: Dataset: TriviaQA with gold passages; Baseline: dense retriever + LM; Variant: LM‑only passage ranking; Metric: Retrieval accuracy and downstream answer exact match.

ETHICAL CONCERNS

This work aims to improve the factuality of LLM outputs, the lack of which continues to cause numerous real-world problems (e.g., spread of misinformation and provision of incorrect and dangerous advice). While our method shows significant improvements in terms of performance, factuality, and citation accuracy, it can still generate outputs that are not fully supported by the citations. We hope that explicit self-reflection and fine-grained attribution may help users verify factual errors in the model outputs.

sources.text: State-of-the-art LLMs continue to struggle with factual errors (Mallen et al., 2023; Min et al., 2023) despite their increased model and data scale (Ouyang et al., 2022). Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) methods (Figure 1 left; Lewis et al. 2020; Guu et al. 2020) augment the input of LLMs with relevant retrieved passages, reducing factual errors in knowledge-intensive tasks (Ram et al., 2023; Asai et al., 2023a). However, these methods may hinder the versatility of LLMs or introduce unnecessary or off-topic passages that lead to low-quality generations (Shi et al., 2023) since they retrieve passages indiscriminately regardless of whether the factual grounding is helpful. Moreover, the output is not guaranteed to be consistent with retrieved relevant passages (Gao et al., 2023) since the models are not explicitly trained to leverage and follow facts from provided passages.

sources.text: Retrieval setup details. By default, we use Contriever-MS MARCO to retrieve the top five documents from Wikipedia, and use official Wikipedia embeddings based on 2018 English Wikipedia. On PopQA, where question and answer pairs are created based on WikiData in 2022, we found that the 2018 Wikipedia sometimes lacks articles about some entities that have been more recently added to Wikipedia. Therefore, for PopQA, we used the December 2020 preprocessed Wikipedia corpus provided by Izacard et al. (2022b) and generated document embeddings.8 The issues of performance variance from different Wikipedia dumps have been reported by prior work (Asai et al., 2020; Izacard et al., 2022b). Yet, we observe limited effectiveness of such off-the-shelf retrieval models trained primarily on knowledge-intensive tasks for open-ended generation (e.g., instruction following).

Compared Systems Contriever models, Contriever and mContriever, serve as our major baseline. They are trained using unsupervised contrastive learning. HyDE retrievers share the exact same embedding spaces with them. The only difference is how the query vector is built. These comparisons allow us to easily examine the effect of HyDE. The classical heuristic-based lexical retriever BM25 is also included.

Short-form generations tasks include two open-domain question answering (QA) datasets, PopQA (Mallen et al., 2023) and TriviaQA-unfiltered (Joshi et al., 2017), where systems need to answer arbitrary questions about factual knowledge. For PopQA, we use the long-tail subset, consisting of 1,399 rare entity queries whose monthly Wikipedia page views are less than 100. As the TriviaQA-unfiltered (open) test set is not publicly available, we follow prior work’s validation and test split (Min et al., 2019; Guu et al., 2020), using 11,313 test queries for evaluation. We evaluate performance based on whether gold answers are included in the model generations instead of strictly requiring exact matching, following Mallen et al. (2023); Schick et al. (2023).

4.3 Low Resource Retrieval

In Table 2, we show retrieval results on lowresource tasks from BEIR. Similar to web search, HyDE again brings sizable improvements to Contriever across the board in terms of both ndcg and recall. HyDE is only outperformed by BM25 on one dataset, TREC-Covid but with a tiny 0.2 margin; in comparison, the underlying Contriever underperforms by more than 50%.

We also observe HyDE demonstrates strong performance compared to fine-tuned models. HyDE generally shows better performance than ANCE and DPR, even though the two are fine-tuned on MS-MARCO and ANCE also involves some sophisticated hard negative techniques. sources.text: ment. Dense retrievers consider vector similarities while self-attentive re-rankers regression scores. In comparison, the concept of relevance in HyDE is captured by an NLG model and the language generation process. We demonstrate in many cases, HyDE can be as effective as dense retrievers that learn to model numerical relevance scores. So, is numerical relevance just a statistical artifact of language understanding? Will a weak retriever theoretically suffice as the NLU & NLG models rapidly become stronger? Rushing to conclusions is not smart; more works need to be done to get answers. With this paper, we just want to raise these questions.
